1  Date : 27/02/2026  ORAL ORDER (PER : HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE BHARGAV D. KARIA)
1. Heard Party in person Mrs. Gnaneshwary Dushyantkumar Shah for the applicant and learned Assistant Government Pleader Ms. Shrunjal Shah for the respondent.
2.

This application is preferred under Section 5 of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/6109/2025 ORDER DATED: 27/02/2026 undefined Limitation Act, 1963 to condone the delay of 1350 days in preferring Miscellaneous Civil Application for Review in Miscellaneous Civil Application No. 89 of 2021 in Letters Patent Appeal No. 128 of 2016 in Special Civil Application No. 9250 of 2013.

3. Party in person, the applicant submitted that the order in Miscellaneous Civil Application No. 89 of 2021 for contempt was passed on 07.02.2022 and thereafter around April, 2025, the applicant was made aware about the initiation of Departmental Inquiry in 2017 which has no bearing on promotion from the deemed date being 22.11.2001 as no Departmental Inquiry was pending against the applicant on the said date.
The applicant, therefore preferred an RTI application on 02.05.2025 seeking information regarding consideration pertaining to confidential report, etc., which was replied on 04.05.2025.
The petitioner thereafter obtained the Government Resolution dated 05.09.1984 which indicates that eligibility of the employee at the relevant time of deemed date is taken into consideration.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/6109/2025 ORDER DATED: 27/02/2026 undefined 4.
In view of such facts, it was submitted that the applicant has preferred this application after a delay of 1350 days.

5. On the other hand, learned AGP Ms. Shrunjal Shah for the respondent submitted that the applicant has failed to provide any sufficient cause to condone the delay of 1350 days in preferring the application for Review.

It was submitted that while disposing Miscellaneous Civil Application No. 89 of 2021 under the provisions of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, the Division Bench of this Court has also observed that the deemed date of promotion shall be subject to the outcome of Special Civil Application No. 2414 of 2017 in which the initiation of the disciplinary proceedings has been questioned by the applicant.

6. It was therefore submitted that merely because the applicant has come to know about the Government Resolution of 1984 after receipt of the reply dated 04.05.2025, it cannot be considered as a sufficient cause NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/6109/2025 ORDER DATED: 27/02/2026 undefined to condone the delay.
In support of her submission, learned AGP Ms. Shrunjal Shah preferred to rely upon the following averments made in the affidavit in reply:

"7. I respectfully submit that once the Oral Order dated 07.02.2022 passed by this Hon'ble Court has been subjected to judicial scrutiny before the Hon'ble Supreme Gnaneshwary Dushyantkumar Shah vs Anju Sharma (Ias), Principal ...

sentences.text: In view of the doctrine of merger and the settled principle of law, no application seeking recall, review, or modification of the said order is maintainable before this Hon'ble Court.

It is well settled that a High Court becomes functus officio in respect of an order which has been affirmed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, and any attempt to seek recall thereof amounts to an impermissible collateral challenge to a final judgment of the Apex Court.
The present application, therefore, is ex facie not maintainable and deserves to be rejected on this ground alone.
8. Further it is submitted in the case of Basawraj and another us.

Special Land Acquisition Officer, 2013 (14) SCC 81 the Apex Court has observed that,
15.

"The law on the issue can be summarised to the effect that where a case has been presented in the court beyond limitation, the applicant has to explain the court as to what was the "sufficient cause" which means an adequate and enough reason which prevented him to approach the court within limitation.

In case a party is found to be negligent, or for want of bona fide on his part in the facts and circumstances of the case, or found to have not acted diligently or remained inactive, NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/6109/2025 ORDER DATED: 27/02/2026 undefined there cannot be a justified ground to condone the delay.
No court could be justified in condoning such an inordinate delay by imposing any condition whatsoever.
The application is to be decided only within the parameters laid down by this Court in regard to the condonation of delay.

In case there was no sufficient cause to prevent a litigant to approach the court on time condoning the delay without any justification, putting any condition whatsoever, amounts to passing an order in violation of the statutory provisions and it tantamount to showing utter disregard to the legislature."

9. I submit that in the case of Majji Sannemma alias Sanyasirao Vs Reddy Sridevi and Others, 2021 SCC OnLine SC 1260 the apex court held:
"16.

sentences.text:
At this stage, a few decisions of this Court on delay in filing the appeal are referred to and considered as under:
17.
In the case of Ramlal, Motilal and Chhotelal(supra), it is observed and held as under:-
In construing s. 5 it is relevant to bear in mind two important considerations.

The first consideration is that the expiration of the period of limitation prescribed for making an appeal gives rise to a right in favour of the decree-holder to treat the decree as binding between the parties.

In other words, when the period of limitation prescribed has expired the decree-holder has obtained a benefit under the law of limitation to treat the decree as beyond challenge, and this legal right which has accrued to the decree- holder by lapse of time should not be light- heartedly Gnaneshwary Dushyantkumar Shah vs Anju Sharma (Ias), Principal ...

3 disturbed.
The other consideration which cannot be ignored is that if sufficient cause for excusing delay is shown discretion is given to the Court to condone delay and admit the appeal.

This discretion has been deliberately conferred on the Court in order NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/6109/2025 ORDER DATED: 27/02/2026 undefined that judicial power and discretion in that behalf should be exercised to advance substantial justice.

As has been observed by the Madras High Court in Krishna v.Chattappan, (1890) J.L.R. 13 Mad. 269, "s. 5 gives the Court a discretion which in respect of jurisdiction is to be exercised in the way in which judicial power and discretion ought to be exercised upon principles which are well understood; the words 'sufficient cause' receiving a liberal construction so as to advance substantial justice when no negligence nor inaction nor want of bona fide is imputable to the appellant.""
10.

I further submit that, in view of the foregoing facts-particularly the petitioner's deliberate and prolonged inaction in pursuing any appellate remedy for more than 3 years-the present application for condonation of delay is a futile exercise.
It appears to be a calculated attempt to unnecessarily burden and vex the respondent- State authority.

The extraordinary delay causes undue prejudice to the principle of administrative finality and seriously undermines the settled norms of service jurisprudence further submit that, in view of the foregoing facts-particularly the petitioner's deliberate and prolonged inaction in pursuing any appellate remedy for over more than 3 years-the present application for condonation of delay is a futile exercise.
It appears to be a calculated attempt to unnecessarily burden and vex the respondent-State authority.

The extraordinary delay causes undue prejudice to the principle of administrative finality and seriously undermines the settled norms of service jurisprudence."
7.

Learned AGP Ms. Shrunjal Shah has also referred and relied upon the order passed by this Court on NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/6109/2025 ORDER DATED: 27/02/2026 undefined 24.02.2026 in Civil Application No. 310 of 2026 for condonation of delay in Letters Patent Appeal No. 36021 of 2025 in Special Civil Application No. 785 of 2019, wherein it was observed that there was no sufficient cause to condone the delay in preferring the Letters Patent Appeal as the lump sum compensation was set aside by the learned Single Judge directing the respondent to reinstate the applicant with continuity of service and therefore, there was no question of awarding any back wages.
8.

Having heard the learned advocates for the respective parties and considering the facts of the case, we are of the opinion that the delay of 1350 days has been sufficiently explained by the applicant in view of the reply dated 04.05.2025 received by the applicant in RTI application and considering that the applicant has subsequently also referred to the Government Resolution dated 05.09.1984.
9.
The application is therefore allowed.
